name: haiku-3
how: Each session: a fresh Claude Code subagent that could read only the rendered prompts (one file per case), answered them in order and wrote its answers to a file. No API key; nothing else in its context.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: The test only checks the URL before clicking Cancel and has no assertion after the click, so nothing verifies the return to the cart.

answers.test: cancel returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: The test clicks Cancel and asserts the URL matches inventory.html.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: The test navigates to /inventory.html after logout and asserts the exact error text.

answers.test: cart badge is cleared after finishing @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the cart badge count is 0 after finishing.

answers.test: removing a product decrements the badge @regression
answers.reason: The test removes one of two items and asserts the badge reads 1.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the URL is inventory.html and the page title is Products after reset.

answers.test: clicking a product name opens its details page @smoke
answers.reason: The test clicks a product name link and asserts the URL contains inventory-item.html?id=4, which is one example as the criterion allows.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: The test captures the list name and price, opens the item, and asserts the details page shows the same values.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts only that an error is visible and never checks that it contains the named text.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts only that the total label contains 'Total: $' and never checks the amount $32.39.

answers.test: item stays in the cart after opening another product @smoke
answers.reason: The test opens another product's details page, returns to the cart, and asserts the backpack is still listed.

answers.test: valid credentials redirect to the products page @smoke
answers.reason: The test logs in with valid credentials and asserts the URL matches inventory.html.

answers.test: logout returns to the login page @smoke
answers.reason: The URL assertion uses the regex /$/, which matches any URL, so it would pass whether or not the login page was reached.
The only test asserting the badge is hidden is marked test.skip, so no test that runs checks this criterion.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The test fills only the first name, continues, and asserts the exact 'Error: Last Name is required' text.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: The product count is checked only after the high-to-low sort, not after every sort the criterion names.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: The test clicks login with no credentials and asserts the error contains 'Username is required'.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the total label text is exactly 'Total: $32.39'.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: The count assertion is a non-awaited check that the count is at least 0, which passes regardless of the number of products.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test sorts low to high and asserts the first item name is Sauce Labs Onesie and its price is $7.99.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The test continues with no first name and asserts the exact 'Error: First Name is required' text.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the first item name is Sauce Labs Onesie but never checks the $7.99 price.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the tax label text is exactly 'Tax: $2.40'.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the visible text 'Epic sadface: Username is required' appears, which contains the named message.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: The test opens the cart after reset and asserts zero inventory items are shown.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the URL is checkout-complete.html and the Checkout: Complete! text is visible.

answers.test: adding a product sets the cart badge to 1 @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts only that the badge is visible and never checks that its count is 1.

answers.test: overview lists the backpack @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the overview's item names are exactly ['Sauce Labs Backpack'].

answers.test: adding a product sets the cart badge to 1 @smoke
answers.reason: The test adds one product and asserts the badge text is 1.

answers.test: locked-out user sees a locked-out message @regression
answers.reason: The test logs in as locked_out_user and asserts the error contains 'Sorry, this user has been locked out'.

answers.test: logout returns to the login page @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the URL equals the base URL after logout.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: The test adds then removes the only item and asserts the badge count is 0.

answers.test: all fields filled continues to the overview @regression
answers.reason: The test fills all three fields, continues, and asserts the title is Checkout: Overview.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The test adds a second item, opens the cart, and asserts the item names match the expected list.

answers.test: item total is $29.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the subtotal label text is exactly 'Item total: $29.99'.

answers.test: missing postal code shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The test fills first and last name, continues, and asserts the exact 'Error: Postal Code is required' text.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: The test clicks Cancel on the information step and asserts the URL matches cart.html.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: The test adds two different products and asserts the badge text is 2.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the title text is exactly 'Checkout: Complete!' after finishing.

answers.test: cart page lists the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The test adds two items, opens the cart, and asserts the exact item names are listed.

answers.test: name Z to A shows the red T-shirt first @regression
answers.reason: The test sorts Z to A and asserts the first item name is Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red).

answers.test: back home returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: The test clicks Back Home and asserts the URL matches inventory.html.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the login button is visible after logout.

answers.test: default sort is name A to Z with Sauce Labs Backpack first @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the sort value is az and the first product is Sauce Labs Backpack on the default page.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: The test only checks the captured list name is truthy and the price contains $, never comparing against the details page.

answers.test: checkout opens the Your Information step @smoke
answers.reason: The test clicks Checkout from the cart and asserts the title is Checkout: Your Information.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: The test submits a wrong password but contains no assertion on the error message.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the page title is Products instead of checking that the badge is hidden.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: The test submits a wrong password and asserts the error contains 'Username and password do not match'.

answers.test: back to products returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: The test clicks Back to products from the details page and asserts the URL matches inventory.html.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts only that the burger menu is visible and never checks the products page URL or title.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts only that the cart holds 2 items and never checks their names.

answers.test: products page displays at least one product after login @regression
answers.reason: The test logs in and asserts the first inventory item is visible.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: The test opens the item, clicks Add to cart, and asserts the badge text is 1.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test sorts high to low and asserts the first name is Sauce Labs Fleece Jacket and its price is $49.99.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the error only contains the word 'required' and never checks the full 'Error: Last Name is required' text.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The test adds a second item, opens the cart, and asserts the exact item names.

answers.test: reset removes the cart badge @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the cart badge count is 0 after Reset App State.

answers.test: thank-you heading is shown @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the complete header text is exactly 'Thank you for your order!'.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: The regex /2.4/ is unanchored and its dot matches any character, so it only checks a fragment of the expected 'Tax: $2.40' text.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The only assertion is wrapped in a try/catch that swallows failures, so the test passes whether or not the login button becomes visible.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: The expect(...).toHaveText('2') call is not awaited, so it never fails the test and the badge count is not actually checked.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: It counts elements matching data-test="cart-item", which is not a usual attribute on the cart page, so toHaveCount(0) matches nothing and passes regardless of the cart contents.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: The badge assertion only runs inside an if-block when the badge is visible, so the test passes when no badge appears at all.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the error is not the 'Last Name is required' message and never checks for the named 'Error: First Name is required' text.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: It reloads the products page via goto and asserts the cart badge text is '1' after the backpack was added.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: It selects the low-to-high sort but checks the last item and its $49.99 price, which reaches the same arrangement as high-to-low (Fleece Jacket first) by a different route, so it counts.
